In the meantime I verified that the commands have nothing to do with it (and therefore neither does `ConsoleIntegrationTestTrait`).

To exclude my environment too, I directly extended `Cake\TestSuite\TestCase`.

It does this with any table:
```php

class FetchMailsCommandTest extends \Cake\TestSuite\TestCase
{
    #[RunInSeparateProcess]
    public function testExecute(): void
    {
        debug($this->fetchTable('MailBoxes')->getConnection()->configName());
    }

    public function testExecute2(): void
    {
        debug($this->fetchTable('MailBoxes')->getConnection()->configName());

}
```

I close the issue, in the absence of other elements and not being able to allow to reproduce. I am quite sure, at this point, that there is some hidden problem in my configuration. If I find something interesting, I will update
@markstory Did you create a test we can commit or is it not something that fits into our test suite?

> Did you create a test we can commit or is it not something that fits into our test suite?

I don't see a reason why I can't open a pull request with what I put together. Perhaps I've missed something.
Interesting, in adding the test from https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/18733#issuecomment-2955167868 into the core tests, I'm able to reproduce the problem. I'll dig deeper.

While I was able to reproduce this, I don't know how to go about fixing it. I was able to verify that the child process does not have the correct connection aliases defined, which is why the query is using the `default` database.

I've tracked down the `RunInSeparateProcess` logic to [SeparateProcessTestRunner](https://github.com/sebastianbergmann/phpunit/blob/main/src/Framework/TestRunner/SeparateProcessTestRunner.php#L37) which renders a [template](https://github.com/sebastianbergmann/phpunit/blob/main/src/Framework/TestRunner/templates/method.tpl) to generate code that is run in a child process. This child process does not fire the `PHPUnitStarted` event that our fixture system uses to setup connection aliases. I didn't see any obvious places where PHPUnit would make it accessible for us to integrate into the isolated process without potentially creating other problems.

The only reasonable solution I can come up with is to define the aliases at the test level, or in `tests/bootstrap.php`. We could provide a method on `Cake\TestSuite\TestCase` to make this easier to do, or make `ConnectionHelper` public, but I don't have a better solution for this as extending PHPUnit internals is hard for us to maintain.

> While I was able to reproduce this, I don't know how to go about fixing it. I was able to verify that the child process does not have the correct connection aliases defined, which is why the query is using the `default` database.

Incredible! Thank you man.

> This child process does not fire the PHPUnitStarted event that our fixture system uses to setup connection aliases.

And can this be considered normal?
I, who am ignorant, would normally expect that a test executed in a child process, "follows" the steps of the others.

To me it seems like a wrong behavior of phpunit, then you say that you know more.

> The only reasonable solution I can come up with is to define the aliases at the test level, or in `tests/bootstrap.php`. We could provide a method on `Cake\TestSuite\TestCase` to make this easier to do, or make `ConnectionHelper` public

In the meantime, it could be a starting point.

> extending PHPUnit internals is hard for us to maintain.

No, please! :satisfied: It would be a terrible thing.
We might have to accept limitations of using RunInSeparateProcess, but I think that will be hard to document clearly and users would run into this issue before finding that.

Mmh.

I try to think out loud. You tell me.

**The problem**: with the `RunInSeparateProcess` attribute, the `PHPUnitStarted` event, which then takes care of set up the connections, is not triggered.

First observation: in addition to [`RunTestsInSeparateProcesses`](https://docs.phpunit.de/en/10.5/attributes.html#runtestsinseparateprocesses) there is also [`RunClassInSeparateProcess`](https://docs.phpunit.de/en/10.5/attributes.html#runclassinseparateprocess) (which runs the entire test class in a separate process).
At this point I imagine the problem is the same (I don't know, I've never used it and I haven't verified it yet, I'm just thinking).

And then, is there anything else? I don't know. PHPUnit actually provides a lot of things and I doubt that anyone uses them all and knows them all. Could there be other cases where it is not triggered? Maybe no, but it's possible.

**Can these unwanted and hardly predictable behaviors be dangerous?**
In my ignorance, I think so. Obviously I personally had no problems, because in my case even the `default` connection does not use the real production database at all.

Let's imagine someone does something like this (I have not verified the correctness of the code):

```php
#[RunInSeparateProcess]
public function testSomeMethod(): void
{
        //In this test, for some reason, I need to remove several records that are normally present as fixtures, because for this test I need them not to exist.
        $Table1->deleteAll(['Articles.status' => 'active']);
        $Table2->deleteAll(['Comments.user_id' => 1]);

        //Here I do some tests for which I needed to truncate the tables
}
```

Obviously, for something done so badly, the responsibility is individual, but the crux of the problem could also be this.

**How to effectively document this stuff?**

"Hey, 1) normally and in most cases CakePHP together with PHPUnit will take care of correctly configuring the connection for the tests, but 2) in some cases (some known, some perhaps not yet known) this might not happen, due to some PHPUnit behaviors".

Maybe it's my fault that I don't know how to document (conceptually for now) effectively.

It could become a little "niche" (Italian term) here:
https://book.cakephp.org/5/en/development/testing.html#test-connections
or somewhere similar, but with little effectiveness.

Let's get to my specific case (I'm a manager of doctors, maybe it can be useful to understand how a non-programmer by profession thinks): my app is now very large, it does many things in different ways, the tests need child processes. Furthermore, given its current size, I'm also thinking of starting to split the data into multiple databases... at this point, I think I'd rather let go of everything, even unhook the tests from the event (and from anything that should take care of the connections) and in my bootstrap manually configure, precisely and transparently the connections I need to use (without delegations).

**Conclusion**: I would say for now (short term) do nothing, just document (as we can, for the reason already explained).
For the future (long term, maybe 6.0, I don't know about that): find a way for the test connections to be set up clearly in the bootstrap file (and nowhere else).
This will obviously require everyone to waste some time and do some boring things, but this may require everything to be transparent and "managed" completely by the test writer.

In case someone has the same problem, currently fixed temporarily in `test/bootstrap.php`:
```php
ConnectionHelper::addTestAliases();
```
The class is marked as internal, but currently it is not an issue.
